q: The angular position of a point of a periodic wave is known as the ____. (2026)
e: Phase angle defines the angular position of a point on a periodic wave.

q: The angular position of a point of a periodic wave is known as the ____ angle. (2026)
e: The phase angle represents the angular position of a point on a wave cycle.

q: Wavefront is always perpendicular to the direction of ____. (2026)
e: Light rays indicate the direction of propagation and are perpendicular to the wavefront.

q: A wavefront is a locus of all points having the same ____ in the wave. (2026)
e: By definition, a wavefront consists of all adjacent points vibrating in the same phase.

q: The angular position of a point of a periodic wave is known as the ____. (2024)
e: Phase angle specifies the fraction of a wave cycle completed relative to a reference point.

q: Bright fringe has ____ intensity. (2024)
e: Constructive interference produces bright fringes which correspond to maximum intensity.

q: There are two types of wavefront; plane wavefront and ____. (2025)
e: Wavefronts are categorized based on shape into plane and spherical wavefronts.

q: The distance between two adjacent bright (or dark) fringes is called ____. (2025)
e: Fringe width is defined as the separation between two consecutive bright or dark bands.

q: The angular position of a point of a periodic wave is the ____. (2025)
e: The angular state of vibration at any point on a wave is termed the phase angle.

q: When light passes through a small opening or around an obstacle, it spreads out, a phenomenon known as ____. (2025)
e: Diffraction refers to the bending and spreading of light around obstacles or apertures.

q: An optical device used to separate light into its component wavelengths by diffraction is called ____ grating. (2025)
e: A diffraction grating splits light into its constituent wavelengths using multiple narrow slits.

q: Bright and dark fringes are formed ____. (2025)
c: alternatively (or) on the screen (or) by interference of light (or) by diffraction of light
e: Interference and diffraction patterns result in alternating bright and dark fringes on a screen.

q: There are two types of wavefront: plane wavefront and ____ wavefront. (2025)
e: The two primary geometric types of wave surfaces are plane wavefronts and spherical wavefronts.

q: A diffraction grating can disperse light into its ____ components. (2025)
e: Diffraction gratings spread light out according to its constituent wavelength components.

q: ____ is always perpendicular to the direction of propagation (or) rays. (2025)
e: A wavefront is everywhere perpendicular to the rays that mark the direction of wave propagation.

q: A ____ can disperse light into its wavelength components. (2025)
e: Prisms and diffraction gratings disperse composite light into its individual wavelength spectra.

q: Distance between two ____ bright (or dark) fringes is called the fringe width. (2025)
e: The spacing measured between two consecutive bright or dark fringes is the fringe width.

q: ____ coherent light is used in the double slits experiment. (2026)
e: Monochromatic light provides a single wavelength required for clean interference fringes.

q: ____ light is used in Young's double-slit experiment. (2026)
e: Young's experiment requires light of a single wavelength and constant phase difference.

q: A diffraction grating consists of a large number of parallel slits of the same width separated by equal ____ spaces. (2026)
e: A diffraction grating comprises numerous fine, parallel, equally spaced transparent slits separated by opaque intervals.
